# fa self-configuration

You are reconfiguring fa itself. The config file IS the source of truth: the
CLI settings commands (`/provider`, `/tools`, `/approval`, …) are thin
editors over the same YAML this skill edits. Edit the file, never invent
keys, verify after every edit, and report what changed and when it applies.

## Hard rules

1. **Never invent keys.** Unknown top-level keys are ignored silently; strict
   sections throw `ConfigException` on unknown keys or bad value types and can
   break startup — `mcp:`, `memory:`, `cube:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`,
   `images:`, `models.custom` fields, `ttsr:`. The `tools:` section throws on
   non-boolean values; unknown TOOL ids only warn (and absent capabilities can
   never be force-enabled). Every key you write must come from this document.
2. **Never write API key VALUES into config.yaml.** Config carries key NAMES
   (`apiKeyName:`) only. Values live in the OS secure store (`/key set`) or the
   environment. A key value in YAML is a leaked secret.
3. **Preserve the file.** Edit surgically (the `edit` tool, or `write` only for
   a file you fully own). Keep comments and unrelated keys byte-identical.
4. **Verify after every edit.** Run the `config` tool's `check` op (or
   `fa config check`) and confirm it passes before declaring success. A
   broken file must be detected by you, not discovered at next boot.
5. **Report scope + application.** Every change report states: which file, which
   scope, and whether it applies live or at next boot.

## Config layout and precedence

| File | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.fah/config.yaml` | user (global) | main settings file; loaded by `loadCliConfig` |
| `<project>/.fah/config.yaml` | project | only the `memory:`, `cube:`, `tools:`, `spills:` sections are read from here — each wins over the user file |
| `<project>/.fah/rules.yaml` | project | TTSR stream rules; project rules win name clashes over the `ttsr:` section |
| `<project>/.fah/lsp.json` | project | LSP server map |
| `<project>/.fah/packages.yaml` | project | plugin configuration |
| `~/.dap/config.json` | user | DAP hub identity/channels (written by the `/settings` hub flow, not YAML) |

Project precedence is per section, not per file: `memory:`, `cube:`,
`tools:` and `spills:` are loaded separately from the project file
(`loadProjectMemoryConfig`, `loadProjectCubeSettings`,
`loadProjectToolsConfig`, `loadProjectSpillsConfig`) and win over the
same section in `~/.fah/config.yaml`. All other sections are read from
the user file only.

Project sections are strict: a present-but-invalid section throws
`ConfigException` at startup. A project `.fah/` that does not exist yet is
created with a minimal valid file — never leave a half-written YAML behind
(write to a temp name and rename, or write the full content in one `write`).

## Workflow

1. Read the request; identify the topic section below.
2. Inspect current state: `config` op `get <key>` / `path` (or read the two
   config files — a missing file means defaults, not an error).
3. Make the edit: `config` op `set` (preferred — it validates before
   writing and preserves the rest of the file byte-for-byte). Fall back to
   a surgical file edit (rule 3) only for what `set` cannot express:
   removing a key.
4. Verify: `config` op `check` (rule 4).
5. Report (rule 5), naming the CLI command equivalent that would have made
   the same change.

## The config tool

The primary editing surface on every host — CLI, desktop app, web, iOS —
because it needs no shell and no `fa` process. One tool, four ops over the
same core the human CLI verbs wrap:

| op | args | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `check` | — | validate both config files with the real parsers; prints errors, warnings, notes and a final `config check: ok` / `config check: failed` |
| `path` | — | list the config file locations and whether each exists |
| `get` | `key` | the effective value of a dotted key; project scope wins for `memory`/`cube`/`tools` |
| `set` | `key`, `value`, `scope`? | surgical single-key write; the edited file is validated BEFORE the write, so an invalid value persists nothing |

`set` answers with the file, scope, old → new value, and whether the change
applies live or at next boot — echo that in your report (rule 5). `scope`
defaults by key: `memory`/`cube`/`tools` → the project file (created minimal
when absent), everything else → the user file; pass `global` or `project`
to override. Keys come from the topic sections below — the tool rejects
unknown top-level keys instead of writing them.
`set` also takes LIST-VALUED keys: pass the value as compact JSON (an
array or object) and it is rendered as a yaml block — `customProviders`

`get` reports list-valued keys as the same compact JSON, so the round

entry, get first and re-set the extended list.
`get` of a platform-inapplicable key and `set` of one answer
`not applicable on this host` with the reason — never write there and
never suggest a file edit as a workaround. The stdio members of an MCP
server (`command`/`args`/`env`) need host process spawning: on web and
iOS/Android containers they are refused; configure a remote server via
`mcp.servers.<id>.url` instead. On a host with no home directory (web)
the global scope is refused for every user-file key — only the project
sections (`memory`/`cube`/`tools`) persist there.

- **Warnings**: unknown top-level keys (the runtime silently ignores them;
  the check does not — a typo must not survive) and dead project-file keys.

# Changelog

## 1.0.508


- chore(ci): document the sm-kicker head-completeness codeless-head crash
  (upstream awf#15) — the factory job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` before
  `--arg`/`--argjson`, so a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed
  files: a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff) crashes the
  job with `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4` — even when CI is fully green
  on that head, and the job's own rescue dispatch can never heal exactly
  those heads. Workaround until the upstream fix: keep the branch head
  code-bearing. Live instance: run 37193754301 on head 1fe9b1232.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 — `schedule_message` self-chains no longer die
  silently at the agent-chatter wake cap. The idle inbox-wake gate
  (`InboxWakePolicy`, shared by the CLI and the app hosts) now exempts a
  delivered scheduled self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to)
  from the 10-consecutive-wake streak: a deliberate agent-chosen cadence
  (night watch, periodic sweep) wakes forever, while foreign
  agent-to-agent chatter stays capped (anti-storm REG) and user-kind
  mail always wakes. A 30s cadence floor bounds a zero-delay
  re-schedule spin (E5). Refused wakes are visible (`[mail] wake
  refused`, once per episode) and every lifecycle step is receipted to
  `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`):
  scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed /
  wake_attempted / turn_started / wake_refused. A failed scheduler scan
  (transient `listDir` error) now re-arms at `failureBackoff` with an
  `onError` log instead of silently disarming the delivery heartbeat.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 review round — refusal receipts and the
  visible refusal line are gated once per refusal EPISODE (the latch
  lives in `InboxWakePolicy` next to the streak and re-arms on the same
  resets), so a held gate no longer appends per-tick `wake_attempted`
  rows (~43k duplicate lines/day) and a repeat episode after user input
  is announced and receipted again. The app host receipts its wake path
  (`wake_attempted` / `turn_started` / `wake_refused`) onto the same
  trail — AC4 is no longer CLI-only. A self-reminder adopted across a
  session-id change delivers FROM the live mailbox (from re-addressed
  alongside to), so the resumed chain stays self-shaped and exempt
  instead of falling back to the capped chatter lane. Plugin-only
  pending batches are explicitly classified as chatter (the contract is
  stated, not accidental), the wake cap is single-sourced from
  `InboxWakePolicy.defaultMaxInboxWakeStreak`, and the policy file lost
  a stale copy-pasted `ignore_for_file`.

## 1.0.485


- fix(ci): Daily auto-publish `pub.dev` leg — poll the pub.dev API until it
  reflects the rerun's publish instead of a single read. 2026-09-28: the
  recovery rerun published AND self-verified 1.0.483 (`pub.dev verified`
  at 05:44:11Z), but the leg's one-shot API query 52s later hit a stale
  replica, saw 1.0.482 and false-errored "manual publish needed". Initial
  behind-check now takes three spaced reads (newest wins) so a stale read
  cannot trigger unnecessary recovery either.
- fix(ci): `install-pin-bump` no longer hard-gates on `release-provenance`.
  When provenance FAILED (binaries/signature upload race), the marker job
  was left SKIPPED — and `rerun --failed` never resurrects skipped jobs, so
  the `vpinned` marker stayed stale forever (v1.0.483: the recovery rerun
  went green, the marker never advanced). The job now uses
  `if: always()`; `pin_release.sh`'s own pre-move provenance gate

# Manual App Store review submission (issue #239 Track 2): submits the iOS
# and/or macOS build of an already-processed TestFlight version straight to
# App Store review. Nothing here builds or uploads a binary — the
# `submit_for_review` lanes pre-flight against App Store Connect and fail
# BEFORE any mutation:
#   - the version must exist (create it via store-metadata.yml first)
#   - a processed TestFlight build must exist for the version
#   - a version already in review = green no-op notice (idempotent re-run)
# `confirm` must repeat `version` exactly (fat-finger guard on an
# irreversible-ish action).
#
# Release-after-approval stays a manual ASC click (owner decision for the
# first month): flipping to automatic release is a one-line repo variable,
# APP_STORE_AUTOMATIC_RELEASE=true (E5).
#
# Secrets: only the existing APP_STORE_CONNECT_* — no new credentials.

name: App Store review submission

run-name: "App Store review (${{ inputs.platforms }}): ${{ inputs.version }}"

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'App version to submit (must match a processed TestFlight build, e.g. 1.2.3)'
        required: true
        type: string
      platforms:
        description: 'Platforms to submit'
        required: true
        default: both
        type: choice
        options:
          - ios
          - macos
          - both
      confirm:
        description: 'Type the version string again to confirm'
        required: true
        type: string

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Fat-finger guard
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - name: Confirm must repeat the version
        run: |
          if [ "${{ inputs.confirm }}" != "${{ inputs.version }}" ]; then
            echo "::error::confirm ('${{ inputs.confirm }}') does not equal version ('${{ inputs.version }}') — aborting before any mutation"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Confirmed: submitting version ${{ inputs.version }} (${{ inputs.platforms }}) for App Store review"

  ios:
    name: Submit iOS for App Store review
    needs: guard
    if: inputs.platforms == 'ios' || inputs.platforms == 'both'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: ruby/setup-ruby@14594264cd68ce8a2345dd349bc3d138a4ef85c8 # v1.99.0 (branch head; v1 moves)
        with:
          ruby-version: '3.2'
          bundler-cache: true
          working-directory: flutter_app

      - name: Submit for review (pre-flight fails before any mutation)
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT }}
          APP_STORE_VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
          APP_STORE_CONFIRM: ${{ inputs.confirm }}
        run: bundle exec fastlane ios submit_for_review

  macos:
    name: Submit macOS for App Store review
    needs: guard
    if: inputs.platforms == 'macos' || inputs.platforms == 'both'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: ruby/setup-ruby@14594264cd68ce8a2345dd349bc3d138a4ef85c8 # v1.99.0 (branch head; v1 moves)
        with:
          ruby-version: '3.2'
          bundler-cache: true
          working-directory: flutter_app

      - name: Submit for review (pre-flight fails before any mutation)
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT }}
          APP_STORE_VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
          APP_STORE_CONFIRM: ${{ inputs.confirm }}
        run: bundle exec fastlane mac submit_for_review

- name: Build Android AAB
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          BUILD_NUMBER: ${{ github.run_number }}
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
          ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}
          ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
          ANDROID_STRICT_RELEASE_SIGNING: 'true'
        run: bundle exec fastlane android build_release

      - name: Verify AAB and validate bundle
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          AAB_PATH="flutter_app/build/app/outputs/bundle/storeRelease/app-store-release.aab"
          if [ ! -f "$AAB_PATH" ]; then
            echo "::error::AAB file not found at $AAB_PATH"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "AAB built successfully: $(ls -la $AAB_PATH)"
          # bundletool validate (issue #289 AC3): catches malformed bundles
          # before they ever reach Play's upload pipeline.
          curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o /tmp/bundletool.jar \
            https://github.com/google/bundletool/releases/download/1.17.0/bundletool-all-1.17.0.jar
          java -jar /tmp/bundletool.jar validate --bundle "$AAB_PATH"
          echo "✅ bundletool validate green"
          # 16 KB page-size gate (gh-746, review round 1): re-check every
          # native lib in the PACKAGED bundle — a staging-layout change that
          # silently un-wires the gate fails here instead of at Play upload.
          # The gate lives in its own script so aab-gate-selftest.yml runs
          # the SAME logic against fixture bundles on every PR (gh-798 AC3):
          # AAB layout base/lib/<abi>/*.so, owned named verdict — never an
          # inherited exit code (gh-786).
          bash scripts/verify_aab_native_libs.sh "$AAB_PATH"

      - name: Upload AAB Artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: android-aab
          path: flutter_app/build/app/outputs/bundle/storeRelease/app-store-release.aab
          retention-days: 14

name: Build Android AAB
    needs: version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily watchers' budget arithmetic (#351): gradle AAB
    # + bundletool validate historically ~20m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    if: |
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'none' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != '' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'metadata_only' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'screenshots_only'
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Setup Java
        uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      - name: Setup Flutter
        uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: 'stable'
          cache: true

      # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (flutter_dotenv);
      # newer flutter validates assets at build time, so the placeholder must
      # exist BEFORE flutter pub get (issue #368: aot_android_asset_bundle

{"content":"# gh-1275 — Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: Apps built from fa 1.0.512 shipped the built-in skills (#1151) as
EMPTY directory structures — on iOS the agent found
`.fah/skills/{create-goal,fa-self-config,js-apps}` present but with no
usable SKILL.md content, so the built-in skills were effectively absent
from app sessions (TestFlight build 205, session clip_1791193461546.txt).

**Root cause**: The app-side half of #1151 delivered built-in skills by
SEEDING them from bundled Flutter assets (`flutter_app/assets/skills/`,
`rootBundle.loadString`) into `.fah/skills/` at session boot. The app
bundling copied/created the skill directory STRUCTURE but the SKILL.md
CONTENT never reached the bundle (asset-packaging class of #1227/#1272:
the packaging glob missed the `.md` files), so the seeded directories
were empty/hollow and the on-disk copies shadowed nothing while the
agent saw no skill bodies. Every guard that existed asserted directory
or wiring PRESENCE, never CONTENT — nothing release-gating checked that
a shipped SKILL.md was non-empty.

**Impact**: Any app host (iOS confirmed; macOS/Android/web equally
affected — same seeding code path) had no usable built-in skills. The
CLI was unaffected (repo-adjacent sources, no asset-bundle hop).

**Fix approach**: gh-1164 (already in tree at v1.0.513) removed the
failing mechanism: the last bundled seed (js-apps) was promoted into
the package builtins — every `prompts/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` is
compiled into pure-Dart `builtinSkillFiles` by `scripts/gen_prompts.dart`
and served from `builtin://skills/<name>/SKILL.md` on every host with no
filesystem/asset-bundle dependency, merged last into discovery. What
remains missing for gh-1275 is the **never-again hook (AC3)**: a
release-gating check that each built-in skill ships with a non-empty
SKILL.md (byte floor) in the packaged artifact, wired into the app
release workflows (iOS/Android/macOS/web) fail-fast before any build
minute is spent (gh-798 "Assert TestFlight version floor" pattern), with
the same checker running on every PR (gh-798 selftest pattern). Verified
in-tree: the compiled `builtinSkillFiles` carries all three skills
(create-goal 8306 B, js-apps 72615 B, self-settings 28699 B), discovery
ignores the empty leftover dirs the cleanup intentionally leaves, and
the skills-access consent still never gates builtins (AC4).

# gh-1275: [BUG] Built-in skills (#1151) not packaged into the apps: iOS ships EMPTY skill dirs (create-goal/fa-self-config/js-apps exist, SKILL.md missing) — verify macOS/Android too

## Description

**Evidence** (owner, iOS fa 1.0.512 / TestFlight build 205, session clip_1791193461546.txt, 2026-10-05): user asks the agent «есть ли у тебя скилл как писать js apps и как create goal делать?» → the agent discovers the skill DIRECTORIES exist (`create-goal`, `fa-self-config`, `js-apps` listed) but are EMPTY — «The skill directories exist but are empty. Check maybe SKILL.md is elsewhere?» — so the agent has no usable built-in skills on iOS.

**Shape**: #1151 shipped built-in skills with fa; the app bundling copies/creates the skill directory STRUCTURE but not the SKILL.md CONTENT (or the packaging glob misses .md assets). Owner suspects other platforms are equally affected — macOS/Android/**web** builds need the same check; the CLI (repo-adjacent) works.

**Never-again hook**: this is the same packaging-blindness class as #1227's asset diet — shipped-shape verification must assert CONTENT, not directory presence: a release-gating check that each built-in skill dir contains a non-empty SKILL.md (byte size > some floor) in the packaged artifact.

**Acceptance:**
- AC1: on iOS, the app's agent sees and can invoke the built-in skills (create-goal, fa-self-config, js-apps) — verified on a TestFlight build carrying the fix.
- AC2: macOS + Android + **web** (fa1.dev build) verified the same way (or explicitly excluded with a written reason).
- AC3: packaging regression guard: the release workflow fails if any built-in skill dir ships without a non-empty SKILL.md.
- AC4: skills remain inert-by-default security-wise (discovery respects the skills-access setting on all platforms).

Unassigned per owner. Refs: #1151, #1227 (asset-packaging class), #1272 (the sibling 1.0.512 packaging incident).

# fa self-configuration

You are reconfiguring fa itself. The config file IS the source of truth: the
CLI settings commands (`/provider`, `/tools`, `/approval`, …) are thin
editors over the same YAML this skill edits. Edit the file, never invent
keys, verify after every edit, and report what changed and when it applies.

## Hard rules

1. **Never invent keys.** Unknown top-level keys are ignored silently; strict
   sections throw `ConfigException` on unknown keys or bad value types and can
   break startup — `mcp:`, `memory:`, `cube:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`,
   `images:`, `models.custom` fields, `ttsr:`. The `tools:` section throws on
   non-boolean values; unknown TOOL ids only warn (and absent capabilities can
   never be force-enabled). Every key you write must come from this document.
2. **Never write API key VALUES into config.yaml.** Config carries key NAMES
   (`apiKeyName:`) only. Values live in the OS secure store (`/key set`) or the
   environment. A key value in YAML is a leaked secret.
3. **Preserve the file.** Edit surgically (the `edit` tool, or `write` only for
   a file you fully own). Keep comments and unrelated keys byte-identical.
4. **Verify after every edit.** Run the `config` tool's `check` op (or
   `fa config check`) and confirm it passes before declaring success. A
   broken file must be detected by you, not discovered at next boot.
5. **Report scope + application.** Every change report states: which file, which
   scope, and whether it applies live or at next boot.

## Config layout and precedence

| File | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.fah/config.yaml` | user (global) | main settings file; loaded by `loadCliConfig` |
| `<project>/.fah/config.yaml` | project | only the `memory:`, `cube:`, `tools:`, `spills:` sections are read from here — each wins over the user file |
| `<project>/.fah/rules.yaml` | project | TTSR stream rules; project rules win name clashes over the `ttsr:` section |
| `<project>/.fah/lsp.json` | project | LSP server map |
| `<project>/.fah/packages.yaml` | project | plugin configuration |
| `~/.dap/config.json` | user | DAP hub identity/channels (written by the `/settings` hub flow, not YAML) |

Project precedence is per section, not per file: `memory:`, `cube:`,
`tools:` and `spills:` are loaded separately from the project file
(`loadProjectMemoryConfig`, `loadProjectCubeSettings`,
`loadProjectToolsConfig`, `loadProjectSpillsConfig`) and win over the
same section in `~/.fah/config.yaml`. All other sections are read from
the user file only.

Project sections are strict: a present-but-invalid section throws
`ConfigException` at startup. A project `.fah/` that does not exist yet is
created with a minimal valid file — never leave a half-written YAML behind
(write to a temp name and rename, or write the full content in one `write`).

## Workflow

1. Read the request; identify the topic section below.
2. Inspect current state: `config` op `get <key>` / `path` (or read the two
   config files — a missing file means defaults, not an error).
3. Make the edit: `config` op `set` (preferred — it validates before
   writing and preserves the rest of the file byte-for-byte). Fall back to
   a surgical file edit (rule 3) only for what `set` cannot express:
   removing a key.
4. Verify: `config` op `check` (rule 4).
5. Report (rule 5), naming the CLI command equivalent that would have made
   the same change.

The primary editing surface on every host — CLI, desktop app, web, iOS —
because it needs no shell and no `fa` process. One tool, four ops over the
same core the human CLI verbs wrap:

| op | args | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `check` | — | validate both config files with the real parsers; prints errors, warnings, notes and a final `config check: ok` / `config check: failed` |
| `path` | — | list the config file locations and whether each exists |
| `get` | `key` | the effective value of a dotted key; project scope wins for `memory`/`cube`/`tools` |
| `set` | `key`, `value`, `scope`? | surgical single-key write; the edited file is validated BEFORE the write, so an invalid value persists nothing |

applies live or at next boot — echo that in your report (rule 5). `scope`
defaults by key: `memory`/`cube`/`tools` → the project file (created minimal
when absent), everything else → the user file; pass `global` or `project`

entry, get first and re-set the extended list.

never suggest a file edit as a workaround. The stdio members of an MCP
server (`command`/`args`/`env`) need host process spawning: on web and

`mcp.servers.<id>.url` instead. On a host with no home directory (web)
the global scope is refused for every user-file key — only the project

# Changelog

## 1.0.508


- chore(ci): document the sm-kicker head-completeness codeless-head crash
  (upstream awf#15) — the factory job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` before
  `--arg`/`--argjson`, so a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed
  files: a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff) crashes the
  job with `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4` — even when CI is fully green
  on that head, and the job's own rescue dispatch can never heal exactly
  those heads. Workaround until the upstream fix: keep the branch head
  code-bearing. Live instance: run 37193754301 on head 1fe9b1232.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 — `schedule_message` self-chains no longer die
  silently at the agent-chatter wake cap. The idle inbox-wake gate
  (`InboxWakePolicy`, shared by the CLI and the app hosts) now exempts a
  delivered scheduled self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to)
  from the 10-consecutive-wake streak: a deliberate agent-chosen cadence
  (night watch, periodic sweep) wakes forever, while foreign
  agent-to-agent chatter stays capped (anti-storm REG) and user-kind
  mail always wakes. A 30s cadence floor bounds a zero-delay
  re-schedule spin (E5). Refused wakes are visible (`[mail] wake
  refused`, once per episode) and every lifecycle step is receipted to
  `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`):
  scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed /
  wake_attempted / turn_started / wake_refused. A failed scheduler scan
  (transient `listDir` error) now re-arms at `failureBackoff` with an
  `onError` log instead of silently disarming the delivery heartbeat.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 review round — refusal receipts and the
  visible refusal line are gated once per refusal EPISODE (the latch
  lives in `InboxWakePolicy` next to the streak and re-arms on the same
  resets), so a held gate no longer appends per-tick `wake_attempted`
  rows (~43k duplicate lines/day) and a repeat episode after user input
  is announced and receipted again. The app host receipts its wake path
  (`wake_attempted` / `turn_started` / `wake_refused`) onto the same
  trail — AC4 is no longer CLI-only. A self-reminder adopted across a
  session-id change delivers FROM the live mailbox (from re-addressed
  alongside to), so the resumed chain stays self-shaped and exempt
  instead of falling back to the capped chatter lane. Plugin-only
  pending batches are explicitly classified as chatter (the contract is
  stated, not accidental), the wake cap is single-sourced from
  `InboxWakePolicy.defaultMaxInboxWakeStreak`, and the policy file lost
  a stale copy-pasted `ignore_for_file`.

## 1.0.485


- fix(ci): Daily auto-publish `pub.dev` leg — poll the pub.dev API until it
  reflects the rerun's publish instead of a single read. 2026-09-28: the
  recovery rerun published AND self-verified 1.0.483 (`pub.dev verified`
  at 05:44:11Z), but the leg's one-shot API query 52s later hit a stale
  replica, saw 1.0.482 and false-errored "manual publish needed". Initial
  behind-check now takes three spaced reads (newest wins) so a stale read
  cannot trigger unnecessary recovery either.
- fix(ci): `install-pin-bump` no longer hard-gates on `release-provenance`.
  When provenance FAILED (binaries/signature upload race), the marker job
  was left SKIPPED — and `rerun --failed` never resurrects skipped jobs, so
  the `vpinned` marker stayed stale forever (v1.0.483: the recovery rerun
  went green, the marker never advanced). The job now uses
  `if: always()`; `pin_release.sh`'s own pre-move provenance gate

# Manual App Store review submission (issue #239 Track 2): submits the iOS
# and/or macOS build of an already-processed TestFlight version straight to
# App Store review. Nothing here builds or uploads a binary — the
# `submit_for_review` lanes pre-flight against App Store Connect and fail
# BEFORE any mutation:
#   - the version must exist (create it via store-metadata.yml first)
#   - a processed TestFlight build must exist for the version
#   - a version already in review = green no-op notice (idempotent re-run)
# `confirm` must repeat `version` exactly (fat-finger guard on an
# irreversible-ish action).
#
# Release-after-approval stays a manual ASC click (owner decision for the
# first month): flipping to automatic release is a one-line repo variable,
# APP_STORE_AUTOMATIC_RELEASE=true (E5).
#
# Secrets: only the existing APP_STORE_CONNECT_* — no new credentials.

name: App Store review submission

run-name: "App Store review (${{ inputs.platforms }}): ${{ inputs.version }}"

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'App version to submit (must match a processed TestFlight build, e.g. 1.2.3)'
        required: true
        type: string
      platforms:
        description: 'Platforms to submit'
        required: true
        default: both
        type: choice
        options:
          - ios
          - macos
          - both
      confirm:
        description: 'Type the version string again to confirm'
        required: true
        type: string

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Fat-finger guard
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - name: Confirm must repeat the version
        run: |
          if [ "${{ inputs.confirm }}" != "${{ inputs.version }}" ]; then
            echo "::error::confirm ('${{ inputs.confirm }}') does not equal version ('${{ inputs.version }}') — aborting before any mutation"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Confirmed: submitting version ${{ inputs.version }} (${{ inputs.platforms }}) for App Store review"

  ios:
    name: Submit iOS for App Store review
    needs: guard
    if: inputs.platforms == 'ios' || inputs.platforms == 'both'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: ruby/setup-ruby@14594264cd68ce8a2345dd349bc3d138a4ef85c8 # v1.99.0 (branch head; v1 moves)
        with:
          ruby-version: '3.2'
          bundler-cache: true
          working-directory: flutter_app

      - name: Submit for review (pre-flight fails before any mutation)
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT }}
          APP_STORE_VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
          APP_STORE_CONFIRM: ${{ inputs.confirm }}
        run: bundle exec fastlane ios submit_for_review

  macos:
    name: Submit macOS for App Store review
    needs: guard
    if: inputs.platforms == 'macos' || inputs.platforms == 'both'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: ruby/setup-ruby@14594264cd68ce8a2345dd349bc3d138a4ef85c8 # v1.99.0 (branch head; v1 moves)
        with:
          ruby-version: '3.2'
          bundler-cache: true
          working-directory: flutter_app

      - name: Submit for review (pre-flight fails before any mutation)
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT }}
          APP_STORE_VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
          APP_STORE_CONFIRM: ${{ inputs.confirm }}
        run: bundle exec fastlane mac submit_for_review

- name: Build Android AAB
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          BUILD_NUMBER: ${{ github.run_number }}
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
          ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}
          ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
          ANDROID_STRICT_RELEASE_SIGNING: 'true'
        run: bundle exec fastlane android build_release

      - name: Verify AAB and validate bundle
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          AAB_PATH="flutter_app/build/app/outputs/bundle/storeRelease/app-store-release.aab"
          if [ ! -f "$AAB_PATH" ]; then
            echo "::error::AAB file not found at $AAB_PATH"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "AAB built successfully: $(ls -la $AAB_PATH)"
          # bundletool validate (issue #289 AC3): catches malformed bundles
          # before they ever reach Play's upload pipeline.
          curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o /tmp/bundletool.jar \
            https://github.com/google/bundletool/releases/download/1.17.0/bundletool-all-1.17.0.jar
          java -jar /tmp/bundletool.jar validate --bundle "$AAB_PATH"
          echo "✅ bundletool validate green"
          # 16 KB page-size gate (gh-746, review round 1): re-check every
          # native lib in the PACKAGED bundle — a staging-layout change that
          # silently un-wires the gate fails here instead of at Play upload.
          # The gate lives in its own script so aab-gate-selftest.yml runs
          # the SAME logic against fixture bundles on every PR (gh-798 AC3):
          # AAB layout base/lib/<abi>/*.so, owned named verdict — never an
          # inherited exit code (gh-786).
          bash scripts/verify_aab_native_libs.sh "$AAB_PATH"

      - name: Upload AAB Artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: android-aab
          path: flutter_app/build/app/outputs/bundle/storeRelease/app-store-release.aab
          retention-days: 14

name: Build Android AAB
    needs: version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily watchers' budget arithmetic (#351): gradle AAB
    # + bundletool validate historically ~20m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    if: |
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'none' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != '' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'metadata_only' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'screenshots_only'
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Setup Java
        uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      - name: Setup Flutter
        uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: 'stable'
          cache: true

      # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (flutter_dotenv);
      # newer flutter validates assets at build time, so the placeholder must
      # exist BEFORE flutter pub get (issue #368: aot_android_asset_bundle
      # died on "No file or variants found for asset: .env"). Content mirrors
      # the ci.yml/build-macos.yml incantation — bare `touch` is not enough
      # on ubuntu/flutter 3.47.4.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: flutter_app

{"content":"# gh-1275 — Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: Apps built from fa 1.0.512 shipped the built-in skills (#1151) as
EMPTY directory structures — on iOS the agent found
`.fah/skills/{create-goal,fa-self-config,js-apps}` present but with no
usable SKILL.md content, so the built-in skills were effectively absent
from app sessions (TestFlight build 205, session clip_1791193461546.txt).

**Root cause**: The app-side half of #1151 delivered built-in skills by
SEEDING them from bundled Flutter assets (`flutter_app/assets/skills/`,
`rootBundle.loadString`) into `.fah/skills/` at session boot. The app
bundling copied/created the skill directory STRUCTURE but the SKILL.md
CONTENT never reached the bundle (asset-packaging class of #1227/#1272:
the packaging glob missed the `.md` files), so the seeded directories
were empty/hollow and the on-disk copies shadowed nothing while the
agent saw no skill bodies. Every guard that existed asserted directory
or wiring PRESENCE, never CONTENT — nothing release-gating checked that
a shipped SKILL.md was non-empty.

**Impact**: Any app host (iOS confirmed; macOS/Android/web equally
affected — same seeding code path) had no usable built-in skills. The
CLI was unaffected (repo-adjacent sources, no asset-bundle hop).

**Fix approach**: gh-1164 (already in tree at v1.0.513) removed the
failing mechanism: the last bundled seed (js-apps) was promoted into
the package builtins — every `prompts/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` is
compiled into pure-Dart `builtinSkillFiles` by `scripts/gen_prompts.dart`
and served from `builtin://skills/<name>/SKILL.md` on every host with no
filesystem/asset-bundle dependency, merged last into discovery. What
remains missing for gh-1275 is the **never-again hook (AC3)**: a
release-gating check that each built-in skill ships with a non-empty
SKILL.md (byte floor) in the packaged artifact, wired into the app
release workflows (iOS/Android/macOS/web) fail-fast before any build
minute is spent (gh-798 "Assert TestFlight version floor" pattern), with
the same checker running on every PR (gh-798 selftest pattern). Verified
in-tree: the compiled `builtinSkillFiles` carries all three skills
(create-goal 8306 B, js-apps 72615 B, self-settings 28699 B), discovery
ignores the empty leftover dirs the cleanup intentionally leaves, and
the skills-access consent still never gates builtins (AC4).

**Evidence** (owner, iOS fa 1.0.512 / TestFlight build 205, session clip_1791193461546.txt, 2026-10-05): user asks the agent «есть ли у тебя скилл как писать js apps и как create goal делать?» → the agent discovers the skill DIRECTORIES exist (`create-goal`, `fa-self-config`, `js-apps` listed) but are EMPTY — «The skill directories exist but are empty. Check maybe SKILL.md is elsewhere?» — so the agent has no usable built-in skills on iOS.

**Shape**: #1151 shipped built-in skills with fa; the app bundling copies/creates the skill directory STRUCTURE but not the SKILL.md CONTENT (or the packaging glob misses .md assets). Owner suspects other platforms are equally affected — macOS/Android/**web** builds need the same check; the CLI (repo-adjacent) works.

**Never-again hook**: this is the same packaging-blindness class as #1227's asset diet — shipped-shape verification must assert CONTENT, not directory presence: a release-gating check that each built-in skill dir contains a non-empty SKILL.md (byte size > some floor) in the packaged artifact.

- AC1: on iOS, the app's agent sees and can invoke the built-in skills (create-goal, fa-self-config, js-apps) — verified on a TestFlight build carrying the fix.
- AC2: macOS + Android + **web** (fa1.dev build) verified the same way (or explicitly excluded with a written reason).
- AC3: packaging regression guard: the release workflow fails if any built-in skill dir ships without a non-empty SKILL.md.
- AC4: skills remain inert-by-default security-wise (discovery respects the skills-access setting on all platforms).

Unassigned per owner. Refs: #1151, #1227 (asset-packaging class), #1272 (the sibling 1.0.512 packaging incident).

# fa self-configuration

You are reconfiguring fa itself. The config file IS the source of truth: the
CLI settings commands (`/provider`, `/tools`, `/approval`, …) are thin
editors over the same YAML this skill edits. Edit the file, never invent
keys, verify after every edit, and report what changed and when it applies.

## Hard rules

1. **Never invent keys.** Unknown top-level keys are ignored silently; strict
   sections throw `ConfigException` on unknown keys or bad value types and can
   break startup — `mcp:`, `memory:`, `cube:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`,
   `images:`, `models.custom` fields, `ttsr:`. The `tools:` section throws on
   non-boolean values; unknown TOOL ids only warn (and absent capabilities can
   never be force-enabled). Every key you write must come from this document.
2. **Never write API key VALUES into config.yaml.** Config carries key NAMES
   (`apiKeyName:`) only. Values live in the OS secure store (`/key set`) or the
   environment. A key value in YAML is a leaked secret.
3. **Preserve the file.** Edit surgically (the `edit` tool, or `write` only for
   a file you fully own). Keep comments and unrelated keys byte-identical.
4. **Verify after every edit.** Run the `config` tool's `check` op (or
   `fa config check`) and confirm it passes before declaring success. A
   broken file must be detected by you, not discovered at next boot.
5. **Report scope + application.** Every change report states: which file, which
   scope, and whether it applies live or at next boot.

## Config layout and precedence

| File | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.fah/config.yaml` | user (global) | main settings file; loaded by `loadCliConfig` |
| `<project>/.fah/config.yaml` | project | only the `memory:`, `cube:`, `tools:`, `spills:` sections are read from here — each wins over the user file |
| `<project>/.fah/rules.yaml` | project | TTSR stream rules; project rules win name clashes over the `ttsr:` section |
| `<project>/.fah/lsp.json` | project | LSP server map |
| `<project>/.fah/packages.yaml` | project | plugin configuration |
| `~/.dap/config.json` | user | DAP hub identity/channels (written by the `/settings` hub flow, not YAML) |

Project precedence is per section, not per file: `memory:`, `cube:`,
`tools:` and `spills:` are loaded separately from the project file
(`loadProjectMemoryConfig`, `loadProjectCubeSettings`,
`loadProjectToolsConfig`, `loadProjectSpillsConfig`) and win over the
same section in `~/.fah/config.yaml`. All other sections are read from
the user file only.

Project sections are strict: a present-but-invalid section throws
`ConfigException` at startup. A project `.fah/` that does not exist yet is
created with a minimal valid file — never leave a half-written YAML behind
(write to a temp name and rename, or write the full content in one `write`).

## Workflow

1. Read the request; identify the topic section below.
2. Inspect current state: `config` op `get <key>` / `path` (or read the two
   config files — a missing file means defaults, not an error).
3. Make the edit: `config` op `set` (preferred — it validates before
   writing and preserves the rest of the file byte-for-byte). Fall back to
   a surgical file edit (rule 3) only for what `set` cannot express:
   removing a key.
4. Verify: `config` op `check` (rule 4).
5. Report (rule 5), naming the CLI command equivalent that would have made
   the same change.

## The config tool

The primary editing surface on every host — CLI, desktop app, web, iOS —
because it needs no shell and no `fa` process. One tool, four ops over the
same core the human CLI verbs wrap:

| op | args | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `check` | — | validate both config files with the real parsers; prints errors, warnings, notes and a final `config check: ok` / `config check: failed` |
| `path` | — | list the config file locations and whether each exists |
| `get` | `key` | the effective value of a dotted key; project scope wins for `memory`/`cube`/`tools` |
| `set` | `key`, `value`, `scope`? | surgical single-key write; the edited file is validated BEFORE the write, so an invalid value persists nothing |

`set` answers with the file, scope, old → new value, and whether the change
applies live or at next boot — echo that in your report (rule 5). `scope`
defaults by key: `memory`/`cube`/`tools` → the project file (created minimal
when absent), everything else → the user file; pass `global` or `project`
to override. Keys come from the topic sections below — the tool rejects
unknown top-level keys instead of writing them.
`set` also takes LIST-VALUED keys: pass the value as compact JSON (an
array or object) and it is rendered as a yaml block — `customProviders`
provider entries are settable this way, e.g. `config` op `set`, key
`customProviders`, value
`[{"name":"my-llama","apiType":"openai","baseUrl":"http://localhost:11434/v1","modelId":"llama3"}]`.
`get` reports list-valued keys as the same compact JSON, so the round
trip is get → edit the JSON → set. A whole list is replaced; to add one
entry, get first and re-set the extended list.
`get` of a platform-inapplicable key and `set` of one answer
`not applicable on this host` with the reason — never write there and
never suggest a file edit as a workaround. The stdio members of an MCP
server (`command`/`args`/`env`) need host process spawning: on web and
iOS/Android containers they are refused; configure a remote server via
`mcp.servers.<id>.url` instead. On a host with no home directory (web)
the global scope is refused for every user-file key — only the project
sections (`memory`/`cube`/`tools`) persist there.

Human/script equivalent (thin wrappers over the same service):
`fa config check`, `fa config path`, `fa config get <dotted.key>`,
`fa config set <dotted.key> <value> [--project|--global]`, and
`fa config export-providers [--out <file.fahx>]` (provider-preset export —
the one verb without a config-file write).

## Verification

`config` op `check` (or `fa config check`) validates both files with the
REAL section parsers and prints named diagnostics — this is the mandatory
final step of every edit:

- **What check reports as errors** (non-zero exit / `config check: failed`):
  yaml syntax errors, strict-section schema errors (`mcp:`, `memory:`,
  `cube:`, `tools:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`, `images:`, `roles:`,
  `ttsr:`, `models.custom`, `fabric:`), and bad scalar types — each naming
  file+section.
- **Warnings**: unknown top-level keys (the runtime silently ignores them;
  the check does not — a typo must not survive) and dead project-file keys.
- **At next boot, semantic errors in strict sections are FATAL**:

# Changelog

## 1.0.508


- chore(ci): document the sm-kicker head-completeness codeless-head crash
  (upstream awf#15) — the factory job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` before
  `--arg`/`--argjson`, so a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed
  files: a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff) crashes the
  job with `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4` — even when CI is fully green
  on that head, and the job's own rescue dispatch can never heal exactly
  those heads. Workaround until the upstream fix: keep the branch head
  code-bearing. Live instance: run 37193754301 on head 1fe9b1232.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 — `schedule_message` self-chains no longer die
  silently at the agent-chatter wake cap. The idle inbox-wake gate
  (`InboxWakePolicy`, shared by the CLI and the app hosts) now exempts a
  delivered scheduled self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to)
  from the 10-consecutive-wake streak: a deliberate agent-chosen cadence
  (night watch, periodic sweep) wakes forever, while foreign
  agent-to-agent chatter stays capped (anti-storm REG) and user-kind
  mail always wakes. A 30s cadence floor bounds a zero-delay
  re-schedule spin (E5). Refused wakes are visible (`[mail] wake
  refused`, once per episode) and every lifecycle step is receipted to
  `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`):
  scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed /
  wake_attempted / turn_started / wake_refused. A failed scheduler scan
  (transient `listDir` error) now re-arms at `failureBackoff` with an
  `onError` log instead of silently disarming the delivery heartbeat.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 review round — refusal receipts and the
  visible refusal line are gated once per refusal EPISODE (the latch
  lives in `InboxWakePolicy` next to the streak and re-arms on the same
  resets), so a held gate no longer appends per-tick `wake_attempted`
  rows (~43k duplicate lines/day) and a repeat episode after user input
  is announced and receipted again. The app host receipts its wake path
  (`wake_attempted` / `turn_started` / `wake_refused`) onto the same
  trail — AC4 is no longer CLI-only. A self-reminder adopted across a
  session-id change delivers FROM the live mailbox (from re-addressed
  alongside to), so the resumed chain stays self-shaped and exempt
  instead of falling back to the capped chatter lane. Plugin-only
  pending batches are explicitly classified as chatter (the contract is
  stated, not accidental), the wake cap is single-sourced from
  `InboxWakePolicy.defaultMaxInboxWakeStreak`, and the policy file lost
  a stale copy-pasted `ignore_for_file`.

## 1.0.485


- fix(ci): Daily auto-publish `pub.dev` leg — poll the pub.dev API until it
  reflects the rerun's publish instead of a single read. 2026-09-28: the
  recovery rerun published AND self-verified 1.0.483 (`pub.dev verified`
  at 05:44:11Z), but the leg's one-shot API query 52s later hit a stale
  replica, saw 1.0.482 and false-errored "manual publish needed". Initial
  behind-check now takes three spaced reads (newest wins) so a stale read
  cannot trigger unnecessary recovery either.
- fix(ci): `install-pin-bump` no longer hard-gates on `release-provenance`.
  When provenance FAILED (binaries/signature upload race), the marker job
  was left SKIPPED — and `rerun --failed` never resurrects skipped jobs, so
  the `vpinned` marker stayed stale forever (v1.0.483: the recovery rerun
  went green, the marker never advanced). The job now uses
  `if: always()`; `pin_release.sh`'s own pre-move provenance gate

# Manual App Store review submission (issue #239 Track 2): submits the iOS
# and/or macOS build of an already-processed TestFlight version straight to
# App Store review. Nothing here builds or uploads a binary — the
# `submit_for_review` lanes pre-flight against App Store Connect and fail
# BEFORE any mutation:
#   - the version must exist (create it via store-metadata.yml first)
#   - a processed TestFlight build must exist for the version
#   - a version already in review = green no-op notice (idempotent re-run)
# `confirm` must repeat `version` exactly (fat-finger guard on an
# irreversible-ish action).
#
# Release-after-approval stays a manual ASC click (owner decision for the
# first month): flipping to automatic release is a one-line repo variable,
# APP_STORE_AUTOMATIC_RELEASE=true (E5).
#
# Secrets: only the existing APP_STORE_CONNECT_* — no new credentials.

name: App Store review submission

run-name: "App Store review (${{ inputs.platforms }}): ${{ inputs.version }}"

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'App version to submit (must match a processed TestFlight build, e.g. 1.2.3)'
        required: true
        type: string
      platforms:
        description: 'Platforms to submit'
        required: true
        default: both
        type: choice
        options:
          - ios
          - macos
          - both
      confirm:
        description: 'Type the version string again to confirm'
        required: true
        type: string

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Fat-finger guard
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - name: Confirm must repeat the version
        run: |
          if [ "${{ inputs.confirm }}" != "${{ inputs.version }}" ]; then
            echo "::error::confirm ('${{ inputs.confirm }}') does not equal version ('${{ inputs.version }}') — aborting before any mutation"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Confirmed: submitting version ${{ inputs.version }} (${{ inputs.platforms }}) for App Store review"

  ios:
    name: Submit iOS for App Store review
    needs: guard
    if: inputs.platforms == 'ios' || inputs.platforms == 'both'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: ruby/setup-ruby@14594264cd68ce8a2345dd349bc3d138a4ef85c8 # v1.99.0 (branch head; v1 moves)
        with:
          ruby-version: '3.2'
          bundler-cache: true
          working-directory: flutter_app

      - name: Submit for review (pre-flight fails before any mutation)
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT }}
          APP_STORE_VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
          APP_STORE_CONFIRM: ${{ inputs.confirm }}
        run: bundle exec fastlane ios submit_for_review

  macos:
    name: Submit macOS for App Store review
    needs: guard
    if: inputs.platforms == 'macos' || inputs.platforms == 'both'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: ruby/setup-ruby@14594264cd68ce8a2345dd349bc3d138a4ef85c8 # v1.99.0 (branch head; v1 moves)
        with:
          ruby-version: '3.2'
          bundler-cache: true
          working-directory: flutter_app

      - name: Submit for review (pre-flight fails before any mutation)
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT }}
          APP_STORE_VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
          APP_STORE_CONFIRM: ${{ inputs.confirm }}
        run: bundle exec fastlane mac submit_for_review

stage_test_core() {

  rm -rf coverage
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration

  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --tags integration \

- name: Build Android AAB
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          BUILD_NUMBER: ${{ github.run_number }}
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
          ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}
          ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
          ANDROID_STRICT_RELEASE_SIGNING: 'true'
        run: bundle exec fastlane android build_release

      - name: Verify AAB and validate bundle
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          AAB_PATH="flutter_app/build/app/outputs/bundle/storeRelease/app-store-release.aab"
          if [ ! -f "$AAB_PATH" ]; then
            echo "::error::AAB file not found at $AAB_PATH"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "AAB built successfully: $(ls -la $AAB_PATH)"
          # bundletool validate (issue #289 AC3): catches malformed bundles
          # before they ever reach Play's upload pipeline.
          curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o /tmp/bundletool.jar \
            https://github.com/google/bundletool/releases/download/1.17.0/bundletool-all-1.17.0.jar
          java -jar /tmp/bundletool.jar validate --bundle "$AAB_PATH"
          echo "✅ bundletool validate green"
          # 16 KB page-size gate (gh-746, review round 1): re-check every
          # native lib in the PACKAGED bundle — a staging-layout change that
          # silently un-wires the gate fails here instead of at Play upload.
          # The gate lives in its own script so aab-gate-selftest.yml runs
          # the SAME logic against fixture bundles on every PR (gh-798 AC3):
          # AAB layout base/lib/<abi>/*.so, owned named verdict — never an
          # inherited exit code (gh-786).
          bash scripts/verify_aab_native_libs.sh "$AAB_PATH"

      - name: Upload AAB Artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: android-aab
          path: flutter_app/build/app/outputs/bundle/storeRelease/app-store-release.aab
          retention-days: 14

  submit-android:

    # Issue #344: a wedged self-hosted worker (lost completion report)
    # otherwise holds the slot AND the in_progress status until the 300m
    # daily-publish watcher times out; a job-level timeout lets GitHub
    # fail the run server-side and unblock the pool + watchers.
    timeout-minutes: 90

      github.event.inputs.ios_content != 'none' &&
      github.event.inputs.ios_content != '' &&
      github.event.inputs.ios_content != 'metadata_only' &&
      github.event.inputs.ios_content != 'screenshots_only'

      - name: Update local git mirror
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$MIRROR")"
          if [ ! -d "$MIRROR" ]; then
            git clone --mirror https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR"
          else
            git -C "$MIRROR" fetch origin
          fi

      - name: Checkout repository from local mirror

      # action keeps the SDK at ~/actions-runner-yoloit/flutter-sdk with a
      # .fah-version marker: subsecond reuse when the pin is unchanged,
      # exactly one download per pin bump, no cache POST step at all.
      # Still a pinned 3.47.x install — the runner's hardcoded

      - name: Setup Flutter (self-hosted)

      - name: Assert TestFlight version floor

{"content":"# gh-1275 — Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: Apps built from fa 1.0.512 shipped the built-in skills (#1151) as
EMPTY directory structures — on iOS the agent found
`.fah/skills/{create-goal,fa-self-config,js-apps}` present but with no
usable SKILL.md content, so the built-in skills were effectively absent
from app sessions (TestFlight build 205, session clip_1791193461546.txt).

**Root cause**: The app-side half of #1151 delivered built-in skills by
SEEDING them from bundled Flutter assets (`flutter_app/assets/skills/`,
`rootBundle.loadString`) into `.fah/skills/` at session boot. The app
bundling copied/created the skill directory STRUCTURE but the SKILL.md
CONTENT never reached the bundle (asset-packaging class of #1227/#1272:
the packaging glob missed the `.md` files), so the seeded directories
were empty/hollow and the on-disk copies shadowed nothing while the
agent saw no skill bodies. Every guard that existed asserted directory
or wiring PRESENCE, never CONTENT — nothing release-gating checked that
a shipped SKILL.md was non-empty.

**Impact**: Any app host (iOS confirmed; macOS/Android/web equally
affected — same seeding code path) had no usable built-in skills. The
CLI was unaffected (repo-adjacent sources, no asset-bundle hop).

**Fix approach**: gh-1164 (already in tree at v1.0.513) removed the
failing mechanism: the last bundled seed (js-apps) was promoted into
the package builtins — every `prompts/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` is
compiled into pure-Dart `builtinSkillFiles` by `scripts/gen_prompts.dart`
and served from `builtin://skills/<name>/SKILL.md` on every host with no
filesystem/asset-bundle dependency, merged last into discovery. What
remains missing for gh-1275 is the **never-again hook (AC3)**: a
release-gating check that each built-in skill ships with a non-empty
SKILL.md (byte floor) in the packaged artifact, wired into the app
release workflows (iOS/Android/macOS/web) fail-fast before any build
minute is spent (gh-798 "Assert TestFlight version floor" pattern), with
the same checker running on every PR (gh-798 selftest pattern). Verified
in-tree: the compiled `builtinSkillFiles` carries all three skills
(create-goal 8306 B, js-apps 72615 B, self-settings 28699 B), discovery
ignores the empty leftover dirs the cleanup intentionally leaves, and
the skills-access consent still never gates builtins (AC4).

Unassigned per owner. Refs: #1151, #1227 (asset-packaging class), #1272 (the sibling 1.0.512 packaging incident).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),

# fa self-configuration

You are reconfiguring fa itself. The config file IS the source of truth: the
CLI settings commands (`/provider`, `/tools`, `/approval`, …) are thin
editors over the same YAML this skill edits. Edit the file, never invent
keys, verify after every edit, and report what changed and when it applies.

## Hard rules

1. **Never invent keys.** Unknown top-level keys are ignored silently; strict
   sections throw `ConfigException` on unknown keys or bad value types and can
   break startup — `mcp:`, `memory:`, `cube:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`,
   `images:`, `models.custom` fields, `ttsr:`. The `tools:` section throws on
   non-boolean values; unknown TOOL ids only warn (and absent capabilities can
   never be force-enabled). Every key you write must come from this document.
2. **Never write API key VALUES into config.yaml.** Config carries key NAMES
   (`apiKeyName:`) only. Values live in the OS secure store (`/key set`) or the
   environment. A key value in YAML is a leaked secret.
3. **Preserve the file.** Edit surgically (the `edit` tool, or `write` only for
   a file you fully own). Keep comments and unrelated keys byte-identical.
4. **Verify after every edit.** Run the `config` tool's `check` op (or
   `fa config check`) and confirm it passes before declaring success. A
   broken file must be detected by you, not discovered at next boot.
5. **Report scope + application.** Every change report states: which file, which
   scope, and whether it applies live or at next boot.

## Config layout and precedence

| File | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.fah/config.yaml` | user (global) | main settings file; loaded by `loadCliConfig` |
| `<project>/.fah/config.yaml` | project | only the `memory:`, `cube:`, `tools:`, `spills:` sections are read from here — each wins over the user file |
| `<project>/.fah/rules.yaml` | project | TTSR stream rules; project rules win name clashes over the `ttsr:` section |
| `<project>/.fah/lsp.json` | project | LSP server map |
| `<project>/.fah/packages.yaml` | project | plugin configuration |
| `~/.dap/config.json` | user | DAP hub identity/channels (written by the `/settings` hub flow, not YAML) |

Project precedence is per section, not per file: `memory:`, `cube:`,
`tools:` and `spills:` are loaded separately from the project file
(`loadProjectMemoryConfig`, `loadProjectCubeSettings`,
`loadProjectToolsConfig`, `loadProjectSpillsConfig`) and win over the
same section in `~/.fah/config.yaml`. All other sections are read from
the user file only.

Project sections are strict: a present-but-invalid section throws
`ConfigException` at startup. A project `.fah/` that does not exist yet is
created with a minimal valid file — never leave a half-written YAML behind
(write to a temp name and rename, or write the full content in one `write`).

## Workflow

1. Read the request; identify the topic section below.
2. Inspect current state: `config` op `get <key>` / `path` (or read the two
   config files — a missing file means defaults, not an error).
3. Make the edit: `config` op `set` (preferred — it validates before
   writing and preserves the rest of the file byte-for-byte). Fall back to
   a surgical file edit (rule 3) only for what `set` cannot express:
   removing a key.
4. Verify: `config` op `check` (rule 4).
5. Report (rule 5), naming the CLI command equivalent that would have made
   the same change.

The primary editing surface on every host — CLI, desktop app, web, iOS —
because it needs no shell and no `fa` process. One tool, four ops over the
same core the human CLI verbs wrap:

| op | args | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `check` | — | validate both config files with the real parsers; prints errors, warnings, notes and a final `config check: ok` / `config check: failed` |
| `path` | — | list the config file locations and whether each exists |
| `get` | `key` | the effective value of a dotted key; project scope wins for `memory`/`cube`/`tools` |
| `set` | `key`, `value`, `scope`? | surgical single-key write; the edited file is validated BEFORE the write, so an invalid value persists nothing |

applies live or at next boot — echo that in your report (rule 5). `scope`

never suggest a file edit as a workaround. The stdio members of an MCP

# Changelog

## 1.0.508


- chore(ci): document the sm-kicker head-completeness codeless-head crash
  (upstream awf#15) — the factory job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` before
  `--arg`/`--argjson`, so a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed
  files: a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff) crashes the
  job with `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4` — even when CI is fully green
  on that head, and the job's own rescue dispatch can never heal exactly
  those heads. Workaround until the upstream fix: keep the branch head
  code-bearing. Live instance: run 37193754301 on head 1fe9b1232.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 — `schedule_message` self-chains no longer die
  silently at the agent-chatter wake cap. The idle inbox-wake gate
  (`InboxWakePolicy`, shared by the CLI and the app hosts) now exempts a
  delivered scheduled self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to)
  from the 10-consecutive-wake streak: a deliberate agent-chosen cadence
  (night watch, periodic sweep) wakes forever, while foreign
  agent-to-agent chatter stays capped (anti-storm REG) and user-kind
  mail always wakes. A 30s cadence floor bounds a zero-delay
  re-schedule spin (E5). Refused wakes are visible (`[mail] wake
  refused`, once per episode) and every lifecycle step is receipted to
  `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`):
  scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed /
  wake_attempted / turn_started / wake_refused. A failed scheduler scan
  (transient `listDir` error) now re-arms at `failureBackoff` with an
  `onError` log instead of silently disarming the delivery heartbeat.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 review round — refusal receipts and the
  visible refusal line are gated once per refusal EPISODE (the latch
  lives in `InboxWakePolicy` next to the streak and re-arms on the same
  resets), so a held gate no longer appends per-tick `wake_attempted`
  rows (~43k duplicate lines/day) and a repeat episode after user input
  is announced and receipted again. The app host receipts its wake path
  (`wake_attempted` / `turn_started` / `wake_refused`) onto the same
  trail — AC4 is no longer CLI-only. A self-reminder adopted across a
  session-id change delivers FROM the live mailbox (from re-addressed
  alongside to), so the resumed chain stays self-shaped and exempt
  instead of falling back to the capped chatter lane. Plugin-only
  pending batches are explicitly classified as chatter (the contract is
  stated, not accidental), the wake cap is single-sourced from
  `InboxWakePolicy.defaultMaxInboxWakeStreak`, and the policy file lost
  a stale copy-pasted `ignore_for_file`.

## 1.0.485


- fix(ci): Daily auto-publish `pub.dev` leg — poll the pub.dev API until it
  reflects the rerun's publish instead of a single read. 2026-09-28: the
  recovery rerun published AND self-verified 1.0.483 (`pub.dev verified`
  at 05:44:11Z), but the leg's one-shot API query 52s later hit a stale
  replica, saw 1.0.482 and false-errored "manual publish needed". Initial
  behind-check now takes three spaced reads (newest wins) so a stale read
  cannot trigger unnecessary recovery either.
- fix(ci): `install-pin-bump` no longer hard-gates on `release-provenance`.
  When provenance FAILED (binaries/signature upload race), the marker job
  was left SKIPPED — and `rerun --failed` never resurrects skipped jobs, so
  the `vpinned` marker stayed stale forever (v1.0.483: the recovery rerun
  went green, the marker never advanced). The job now uses
  `if: always()`; `pin_release.sh`'s own pre-move provenance gate

blocks.text:
# Manual App Store review submission (issue #239 Track 2): submits the iOS
# and/or macOS build of an already-processed TestFlight version straight to
# App Store review. Nothing here builds or uploads a binary — the
# `submit_for_review` lanes pre-flight against App Store Connect and fail
# BEFORE any mutation:
#   - the version must exist (create it via store-metadata.yml first)
#   - a processed TestFlight build must exist for the version
#   - a version already in review = green no-op notice (idempotent re-run)
# `confirm` must repeat `version` exactly (fat-finger guard on an
# irreversible-ish action).
#
# Release-after-approval stays a manual ASC click (owner decision for the
# first month): flipping to automatic release is a one-line repo variable,
# APP_STORE_AUTOMATIC_RELEASE=true (E5).
#
# Secrets: only the existing APP_STORE_CONNECT_* — no new credentials.

name: App Store review submission

run-name: "App Store review (${{ inputs.platforms }}): ${{ inputs.version }}"

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'App version to submit (must match a processed TestFlight build, e.g. 1.2.3)'
        required: true
        type: string
      platforms:
        description: 'Platforms to submit'
        required: true
        default: both
        type: choice
        options:
          - ios
          - macos
          - both
      confirm:
        description: 'Type the version string again to confirm'
        required: true
        type: string

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Fat-finger guard
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - name: Confirm must repeat the version
        run: |
          if [ "${{ inputs.confirm }}" != "${{ inputs.version }}" ]; then
            echo "::error::confirm ('${{ inputs.confirm }}') does not equal version ('${{ inputs.version }}') — aborting before any mutation"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Confirmed: submitting version ${{ inputs.version }} (${{ inputs.platforms }}) for App Store review"

  ios:
    name: Submit iOS for App Store review
    needs: guard
    if: inputs.platforms == 'ios' || inputs.platforms == 'both'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: ruby/setup-ruby@14594264cd68ce8a2345dd349bc3d138a4ef85c8 # v1.99.0 (branch head; v1 moves)
        with:
          ruby-version: '3.2'
          bundler-cache: true
          working-directory: flutter_app

      - name: Submit for review (pre-flight fails before any mutation)
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT }}
          APP_STORE_VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
          APP_STORE_CONFIRM: ${{ inputs.confirm }}
        run: bundle exec fastlane ios submit_for_review

  macos:
    name: Submit macOS for App Store review
    needs: guard
    if: inputs.platforms == 'macos' || inputs.platforms == 'both'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: ruby/setup-ruby@14594264cd68ce8a2345dd349bc3d138a4ef85c8 # v1.99.0 (branch head; v1 moves)
        with:
          ruby-version: '3.2'
          bundler-cache: true
          working-directory: flutter_app

      - name: Submit for review (pre-flight fails before any mutation)
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT }}
          APP_STORE_VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
          APP_STORE_CONFIRM: ${{ inputs.confirm }}
        run: bundle exec fastlane mac submit_for_review

- name: Build Android AAB
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          BUILD_NUMBER: ${{ github.run_number }}
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
          ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}
          ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
          ANDROID_STRICT_RELEASE_SIGNING: 'true'
        run: bundle exec fastlane android build_release

      - name: Verify AAB and validate bundle
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          AAB_PATH="flutter_app/build/app/outputs/bundle/storeRelease/app-store-release.aab"
          if [ ! -f "$AAB_PATH" ]; then
            echo "::error::AAB file not found at $AAB_PATH"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "AAB built successfully: $(ls -la $AAB_PATH)"
          # bundletool validate (issue #289 AC3): catches malformed bundles
          # before they ever reach Play's upload pipeline.
          curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o /tmp/bundletool.jar \
            https://github.com/google/bundletool/releases/download/1.17.0/bundletool-all-1.17.0.jar
          java -jar /tmp/bundletool.jar validate --bundle "$AAB_PATH"
          echo "✅ bundletool validate green"
          # 16 KB page-size gate (gh-746, review round 1): re-check every
          # native lib in the PACKAGED bundle — a staging-layout change that
          # silently un-wires the gate fails here instead of at Play upload.
          # The gate lives in its own script so aab-gate-selftest.yml runs
          # the SAME logic against fixture bundles on every PR (gh-798 AC3):
          # AAB layout base/lib/<abi>/*.so, owned named verdict — never an
          # inherited exit code (gh-786).
          bash scripts/verify_aab_native_libs.sh "$AAB_PATH"

      - name: Upload AAB Artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: android-aab
          path: flutter_app/build/app/outputs/bundle/storeRelease/app-store-release.aab
          retention-days: 14

  submit-android:

build-ios:

    # Issue #344: a wedged self-hosted worker (lost completion report)
    # otherwise holds the slot AND the in_progress status until the 300m
    # daily-publish watcher times out; a job-level timeout lets GitHub
    # fail the run server-side and unblock the pool + watchers.
    timeout-minutes: 90
    if: |
      github.event.inputs.ios_content != 'none' &&
      github.event.inputs.ios_content != '' &&
      github.event.inputs.ios_content != 'metadata_only' &&
      github.event.inputs.ios_content != 'screenshots_only'
    steps:
      - name: Update local git mirror
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$MIRROR")"
          if [ ! -d "$MIRROR" ]; then
            git clone --mirror https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR"
          else
            git -C "$MIRROR" fetch origin
          fi

      - name: Checkout repository from local mirror
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          cd /tmp
          rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          echo "Checked out: $(git -C $GITHUB_WORKSPACE log -1 --oneline)"

      # Persistent pinned SDK (issue #354): subosito/flutter-action with
      # cache: true on this PERSISTENT runner cost 5m39s setup (untar ~1GB
      # archive) + 8m47s POST (re-tar the whole SDK) per job — 14.5 of
      # 19.7 min around a 4-min build (run 34815041052). The composite
      # action keeps the SDK at ~/actions-runner-yoloit/flutter-sdk with a
      # .fah-version marker: subsecond reuse when the pin is unchanged,
      # exactly one download per pin bump, no cache POST step at all.
      # Still a pinned 3.47.x install — the runner's hardcoded
      # $HOME/.local/flutter is a stale 3.44.4, below the repo floor
      # >=3.47.0 (daily-publish #260).
      - name: Setup Flutter (self-hosted)
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-flutter-selfhosted
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'

      - name: Setup environment (self-hosted)
        run: |
          echo "/opt/homebrew/opt/ruby/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH
          echo "/opt/homebrew/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH

      # gh-798 AC1/AC2: fail FAST before any build minute is spent when the
      # version about to be stamped is not above ASC's approved floor
